## kb_to_source

- Every normative sentence of the 15 documents in scope (hubs, computation documents, factor documents, the base documents above) traces to a source rule, compute binding, variant parameter or tool docstring. Illustrations, boundary tables and Q&A are hypothetical restatements that entail nothing beyond the source.
- Statements resting on compute bindings rather than rule text, checked for equivalence: `redecision_standards` "The decided assessment is … the account's most recent Superhost assessment" (compute `LATEST(... host_superhost_assessed)`); `suspension_response_proration` "The overturned strike is read from the decision date of the approved policy strike appeal" (compute `date_field='decided_at'`); `earlier_credit_multiples` "whenever it was booked; the credit being worked out is not one of them" (compute `COUNT` of all issued credits before the write). All equivalent; none adds a condition.
- Added confirmations, reviews, notifications, waits or steps: none found.
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …"): none. Each task tool appears in exactly one document (its own hub): `apply_superhost_decision_f25b833f` → `superhost_redecision_fbf3a183`; `claim_superhost_travel_credit_0d8c95c2` → `travel_credit_claims_dacdf014`.
- Task opening world state written as policy fact: none (no document states that any account is suspended, Standard Host, holds two credits, etc.; all figures are labelled hypothetical).

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** No atom unborne, none borne with changed meaning, no claim outside the source; retired surface (4 clauses relevant to this task's policies) written as retired and nothing retired that the source did not retire.

Policy-side notes (not KB verdicts): (1) overwrite 2 of `host_ext_superhost_redecision` retires the base met-clause for every Superhost assessment while its replacement is phrased for "the decision"; the KB renders exactly that, so ordinary quarterly assessments now read their met test from the comparison sheet — a source-layer scoping choice. (2) the enrollment policy's replaced_by ("follows the order of precedence of the tier assignment, except…") references the precedence clause that the same overwrite retires; carried as the source states it.
